From our side, the invoice description and timing matter for our cost allocation.

2) Listing credit visibility: if Redwood issues a listing credit (to reflect a promotional uplift to our MSP partner), will that credit reduce the Marketplace gross charge immediately or show up as a subsequent credit memo?

3) Channel split / margin: our partner requires clarity on the net rev share they will report. Can you confirm typical % splits you expect for a reseller-anchored private offer with the price tiers in the attached spreadsheet?

Attached the draft PO and a simplified pricing model. Can you loop in finance/ops if needed — I cc'd Ben since he was on the prior call.

Thanks Jared — good questions. High level answers below, then a short proposed implementation we can sign off on.

1) Passback mechanics:
- For AWS private offers we typically do passbacks as a Marketplace listing credit when the discount applies at purchase time (i.e., the buyer sees the reduced line item on the AWS charge).
- If the commercial structure requires a downstream rebate to the reseller (post-invoice), we can model that as an offline rebate (credit memo) that Redwood issues to the reseller and Acme, netting via partner agreements.

2) Listing credit visibility:
- Immediate reduction: if the private offer maps to a discounted SKU, AWS shows the discounted price on the invoice line (cleanest for your accounting).
- Credit memo: if you prefer to keep list price intact (for internal benchmarking) but apply an economic credit later, we can issue a credit memo. That will appear on your next billing cycle.

3) Channel split / margin:
- Typical approach for this class of deal: gross revenue credited on the Marketplace at net-of-discount; Redwood remits reseller share as an offline settlement on a monthly cadence (30 days). We can surface a projected passback % by tier — see Ben's note below for the modeled splits.

Proposed implementation (to keep legal comfortable and minimize invoice churn):
- Use SKU-level private offer so AWS reflects the discounted price on purchase (preferred).
- Redwood will issue a separate monthly settlement to the reseller covering their margin (documented in SOW).
- Redwood will provide a monthly CSV settlement extract and an access-controlled S3 link for reconciliation.

Next steps: Ben, can you pull the modeled reseller splits from the attached workbook and confirm the percent by tier? Irene, please advise if the settlement extract needs additional fields for audit (invoice id, SKU, usage units, customer account id).

Markus
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Markus / Jared — quick calc from the spreadsheet (pricing_model_acme_v3.xlsx):

- Tier A (0–250k tokens/month): list price 0.12 /k token, private-offer price 0.09 => discount 25%
  - Reseller passback proposed: 10% of net revenue (i.e., 1.0% of list price grossed, but implemented as 10% of the revenue Redwood records post-discount)
- Tier B (250k–1M): private price 0.075 => discount ~37.5%
  - Reseller passback: 12% of net revenue
- Tier C (>1M): private price 0.06 => discount 50%
  - Reseller passback: 15% of net revenue

Notes on mechanics:
- If Acme wants the AWS invoice to show the "discounted" line item we must create the private offer SKU mapping (preferred). That causes AWS to bill at the reduced price at purchase time; Redwood will then account for "gross" on our books and run a monthly settlement to the reseller for their passback.
- If Acme requires the reseller to receive their split immediately on the Marketplace (i.e., the partner's revenue recognized on the Marketplace invoice rather than a Redwood settlement), we need a partner listing arrangement and that increases complexity (and latency) — we generally avoid unless required.

Deliverables:
- I will export a sample settlement CSV mock (fields: invoice_id, purchase_date, sku, units, gross_amount, discount_applied, net_amount, reseller_share, settlement_id) and drop to the deal ticket.
- Markus/Irene: confirm the field list and whether tax/timestamp needs to be included.

Ben
